acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Minotaurs family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Labyrinth Warrior, T3, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Turning-Wall Specialist (Specialist) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Massive body, horns spreading past the shoulders, chained bronze plate sections, and a greataxe carried one-handed form a mobile labyrinth mechanism.

Signature mechanic: Bronze Turn: the Warrior unhooks one chained plate, plants it as a wall, and pulls the chain around a horn wider than its shoulders to swing the wall ninety degrees; its one-handed greataxe covers only the closing side.
battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the fight by dragging chained bronze plate into a temporary labyrinth wall, redirecting movement before striking around its corner.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe construction: T1 Bull-kin keeps short uncapped horns, a rope harness, wooden maul, and unarmored hide while clay fuel beads and a charred rope wick remain tied to the wood; T2–T5 may add vented horn caps, heat-blued bronze, leather collars, chain, axe, slab, and armor according to their source forms.

Committed attacks drive combustion through the loaded side: the T1 wick smokes along the wooden maul and cools at a planted hoof, while later tiers vent the active capped horn or metal weapon and expose a black harness seam after release.
counterplay: Move through the slack-chain corridor, sever the exposed hinge, or cross the non-axe corner while the wall rotates. Affinity signal: T1 Bull-kin exposes the rope wick on its wooden maul beside the planted hoof before ignition; T2–T5 expose the fuel collar or vented horn cap before the charge and the blackened harness seam during cooldown.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only orange hide or brighter native bronze
Glow-only fire treatment without fuel, venting, combustion, and cooldown
Using the Bull Emperor's family-native brazier-like eye glow alone as Fire affinity
Flame anatomy that obscures horns, hooves, weapon mass, or commitment direction
identityInvariants: A bull head, bovine snout and ears, wide horns, vastly overbuilt humanoid torso, digitigrade hooved legs, and thick tail remain legible at every tier.
Deep russet and black hide, bronze, ox-blood red, and bone define the family palette.
Coarse hair, horn, bronze, heavy leather harness, chain, and hewn stone remain distinct load-bearing materials.
Nose rings, horn caps, brands, arena trophies, and chained slabs communicate rank through visible history and repairs.
Weapon mass and horn spread always preserve a readable commitment direction and recovery side.
telegraph: Chained plate drops from the torso, the chain wraps one broad horn, and the greataxe moves to the side the wall will close.
